target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∃ _ : Theory.RE Def9,
    Def4 Def9.theory ∧ Def2 (Def7 Def9) ∧
      (∼Def7 𝗣𝗔) ∈ Def9.theory ∧ ¬ Def2 (∼Def7 𝗣𝗔)
a_raw: {"translation":"For a recursively enumerable arithmetic axiom set A, write C(A) for the arithmetic sentence saying that no contradiction is provable from the Craig presentation of A. Let B be PA with the single additional axiom ¬C(PA). Target says that there exists a witness that B is recursively enumerable such that, using that witness to form C(B), all four conditions hold: (1) the set of all theorems of B, itself used as an axiom set, does not prove a contradiction; (2) C(B) is true in the standard natural numbers; (3) ¬C(PA) belongs to the set of theorems of B; and (4) that same sentence, ¬C(PA), is not true in the standard natural numbers. Condition (2) does not require B to prove C(B)."}
translation: For a recursively enumerable arithmetic axiom set A, write C(A) for the arithmetic sentence saying that no contradiction is provable from the Craig presentation of A. Let B be PA with the single additional axiom ¬C(PA). Target says that there exists a witness that B is recursively enumerable such that, using that witness to form C(B), all four conditions hold: (1) the set of all theorems of B, itself used as an axiom set, does not prove a contradiction; (2) C(B) is true in the standard natural numbers; (3) ¬C(PA) belongs to the set of theorems of B; and (4) that same sentence, ¬C(PA), is not true in the standard natural numbers. Condition (2) does not require B to prove C(B).

divergences.description: `Def7` uses the consistency sentence of a Craig presentation, both for PA and for `Def9`. This need not be syntactically identical to a consistency sentence built from the original axioms, but the Craig presentation has the same theorems, so it expresses the intended consistency in the standard model.

`Def4 Def9.theory` asserts consistency of the theorems of `Def9` used as axioms, rather than consistency of `Def9` directly. These are equivalent because taking deductive closure does not change what is provable.

judgement.summary: The target gives the claimed standard-model counterexample: `Def9` is recursively enumerable and consistent, its consistency sentence is true, and it proves the false arithmetic sentence `∼Def7 𝗣𝗔`. Thus the quoted implication fails on the arithmetic-truth reading; the target makes no claim about what DTK proves.
